steps.label: billing
steps.sub: the namespace the Service lives in

steps.label: svc
steps.sub: fixed segment — this is a Service record

code:
# kube-system runs CoreDNS, fronted by its own Service
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns
kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns

# resolving payments-api.billing.svc.cluster.local
# returns the Service's stable ClusterIP
caption: Create a Service and CoreDNS already knows how to answer for it — no manual zone file.

eyebrow: Short names depend on the search path
code:
# from a Pod IN the billing namespace, all three work:
payments-api
payments-api.billing
payments-api.billing.svc.cluster.local

# from a Pod in a DIFFERENT namespace (checkout), only this is safe:
payments-api.billing.svc.cluster.local
caption: Each Pod's search path tries its own namespace first — cross-namespace calls need the full name.

eyebrow: Debugging resolution from inside a Pod
code:
kubectl run dnsutils --image=registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/jessie-dnsutils:1.3 \
  --restart=Never -- sleep 3600

kubectl exec -it dnsutils -- nslookup payments-api.billing.svc.cluster.local
kubectl exec -it dnsutils -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
caption: nslookup confirms the IP CoreDNS returns; resolv.conf shows the Pod's actual search path.

subtitle: Everything so far assumed any Pod could reach any Service — next lesson changes that.
